prediction: The Federal Housing Administration (FHA) insures private mortgage lenders against borrower default, enabling access to affordable mortgages for first-time and lower-income homebuyers. FHA-insured mortgages have lower down payment requirements and more lenient credit standards compared to conventional mortgages. FHA's market share fluctuates with economic conditions, peaking at over 30% of home purchase mortgages during the 2007-2009 housing crisis. The FHA Mutual Mortgage Insurance Fund (MMI Fund) is funded through insurance premiums and proceeds from foreclosed homes, with a statutory requirement to maintain a capital ratio of at least 2%. While the fund has historically generated negative credit subsidy, recent years have seen improved financial stability. FHA's role in the mortgage market is countercyclical, providing insurance during periods of economic downturn to support housing access.
